title: Signed lattice-path shuffle boundary identity on unnormalized free simplices
statement:
Use chain complexes of $\mathbf Z$-modules (abelian groups) as in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $p,q\geq0$ be integers. For $a\geq0$, let $U(p)_a$ be the free abelian group of finite integral linear combinations of weakly increasing strings $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_a)$ with $0\leq u_i\leq p$. Set $\partial u=\sum_{i=0}^a(-1)^i(u_0,\ldots,\widehat u_i,\ldots,u_a)$ for $a>0$ and $\partial=0$ in degree zero; let $\epsilon_p:U(p)_0	o\mathbf Z$ send every vertex to $1$. Define $U(q)$ in the same way. Let $V(p,q)_n$ be the free abelian group on coordinatewise weakly increasing strings of $n+1$ pairs in $[p]	imes[q]$, with the same alternating deletion differential, zero in degree zero, and augmentation $\epsilon_V$ sending each pair vertex to $1$. Repetitions are retained in all these groups.

For strings $u\in U(p)_a$, $v\in U(q)_b$, set $n=a+b$. For a partition $\mu\sqcup
u=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with $|\mu|=a$, $|
u|=b$, put $A_k=\#\{j\in\mu:j<k\}$, $B_k=\#\{j\in
u:j<k\}$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Write $\epsilon(\mu,
u)$ for the sign of the permutation obtained by listing $\mu$ and then $
u$, each increasingly. Define
$$\sigma(u\otimes v)=\sum_{\mu,
u}\epsilon(\mu,
u) ig((u_{A_0},v_{B_0}),\ldots,(u_{A_n},v_{B_n}) ig),$$
extended bilinearly, where $U(p)_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}U(q)_b$ is equivalently the free abelian group on pairs $(u,v)$. Then
$$\partial\sigma(u\otimes v)=\sigma(\partial u\otimes v)+(-1)^a\sigma(u\otimes\partial v),\qquad \epsilon_V\sigma_0=\epsilon_p\otimes\epsilon_q.$$
The first identity omits the first term when $a=0$ and the second term when $b=0$. Every pair of monotone maps $[p]	o[p']$, $[q]	o[q']$ commutes with $\sigma$ by postcomposition on the entries.

proof.text: Deletion preserves weak increase. Deleting positions $i<j$ in opposite orders has coefficients $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, hence $\partial^2=0$; in degree one the next differential is zero. An edge boundary has augmentation $1-1=0$. Extending by zero gives the complexes of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Every shuffle term is valid since its coordinate counts are nondecreasing and in range.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle boundary calculation; the blueprint motivates the comparison but supplies no combinatorial proof. The numbered cases below are proved directly from the displayed definitions.

proof.text: Apply the word lemmas with $X=[p]$, $Y=[q]$ and the given strings. Encode the partition by $w\in W_{a,b}$, with $H$ at its horizontal positions. By [lem-sfb-shuffle-mixed-corner-cancellation] the permutation sign is $s(w)=(-1)^{I(w)}$. For $n=a+b>0$, expand the boundary as the finite sum of $s(w)(-1)^k[d_kz_{u,v}(w)]$ over labeled pairs $(w,k)$. Partition these into mixed interior corners, horizontal cases, and vertical cases: endpoints belong to the type of their only adjacent letter, and interiors have either unlike or equal adjacent letters. The mixed sum is zero by the cited involution.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle boundary calculation; the blueprint motivates the comparison but supplies no combinatorial proof. The numbered cases below are proved directly from the displayed definitions.

proof.text: For $a>0$, [lem-sfb-shuffle-horizontal-face-reindexing] bijects every horizontal case, including both endpoints, with $(i,\bar w)\in\{0,\ldots,a\}\times W_{a-1,b}$, preserving its evaluated string and giving coefficient $(-1)^i s(\bar w)$. Thus their sum is $\sigma(\partial u\otimes v)$. For $b>0$, [lem-sfb-shuffle-vertical-face-reindexing] similarly gives coefficient $(-1)^{a+j}s(\bar w)$ and sum $(-1)^a\sigma(u\otimes\partial v)$. When a factor degree is zero its labeled set is empty. All evaluated strings are weakly increasing. Thus coefficients outside the monotone strings are zero on every side; equality on each remaining basis symbol gives the identity in $V(p,q)$. The three disjoint cases exhaust the boundary; repeated generators are collected only afterwards. If $a=b=0$, all differential terms are zero. Bilinearity extends the identity from basis pairs.

proof.text: In degree zero the unique word is empty and has sign $1$, so $\sigma_0$ sends a pair of vertices to that pair vertex. Both augmentations send it to $1$ under $\mathbf Z\otimes\mathbf Z\cong\mathbf Z$. Linearity proves the augmentation identity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle boundary calculation; the blueprint motivates the comparison but supplies no combinatorial proof. The numbered cases below are proved directly from the displayed definitions.

proof.text: For monotone $f,g$, the $w$ summand postcomposes entrywise to $(f(u_{A_k}),g(v_{B_k}))$, exactly the summand obtained by postcomposing the inputs first. Words and signs are unchanged. Sum to obtain naturality. Postcomposition commutes with deletion and takes vertices to vertices, giving augmented chain maps. This remains termwise equality when noninjective maps identify generators.
